description: Authors a durable design-token contract under docs/specs/design/tokens/: a canonical W3C DTCG 2025.10 JSON file ($value/$type, {group.token.path} aliases pinned to /tr/2025.10/, never /tr/drafts/), reusing an existing design system before inventing a brand, enforcing WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (never meaning by colour alone), with an optional version-pinned/runtime-probed alpha DESIGN.md always paired with the DTCG JSON. Single-file by default. Writes no application code.

evals.prompt: We're greenfield with no design system yet. Define our core design tokens (colours, spacing, radius, type) and check contrast. I approve writing the token file now — proceed.
assertions: Creates a single canonical DTCG file at docs/specs/design/tokens/tokens.dtcg.json — not a multi-file token tree
The JSON is DTCG 2025.10 shape: tokens use $value and $type, groups carry an inheritable $type, and references use {group.token.path} aliases that resolve with no cycles
The token format is pinned to https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/ and never references /tr/drafts/
A contrast report is produced and every declared foreground/background pair meets WCAG 2.2 AA (>=4.5:1 normal text); no palette that fails contrast is approved
No status/semantic meaning is carried by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1 is respected)
No application or source-code files are created and no leftover {{placeholder}} remains

evals.prompt: Our repo already uses Tailwind and shadcn/ui. Set up our design tokens. You're approved to write the file now.
assertions: Detects the existing Tailwind/shadcn design system before proposing any tokens (scans tailwind.config / components.json / CSS custom properties)
Adopts or extends the existing token values rather than replacing them with a freshly invented brand palette
Emits the tokens as canonical DTCG 2025.10 JSON at docs/specs/design/tokens/tokens.dtcg.json as the single source of truth
States explicitly that it reused the existing system rather than inventing a new one
No application or source-code files are created

evals.prompt: Approve this palette for us: body text #999999 on a white #ffffff background, and show error state using red text only. I approve writing it now.
assertions: Runs a contrast check and flags #999999 on #ffffff as failing WCAG 2.2 AA for normal text (ratio below 4.5:1)
Does NOT approve the palette as-is; recommends a darker text token that passes AA and re-checks
Flags that conveying the error state by red colour alone violates WCAG 1.4.1 and requires a second channel (icon, text label, or pattern)
Targets WCAG 2.2 AA explicitly and does not introduce WCAG 3.0 or APCA contrast
No application or source-code files are created

evals.prompt: Define our tokens and also give me a Google Labs design.md file for them. I approve writing the files now.
assertions: Produces the canonical DTCG 2025.10 tokens.dtcg.json as the source of truth
Any DESIGN.md produced carries an ALPHA / 'the format will change' banner and a pinned spec/CLI version in its frontmatter
The DESIGN.md is emitted alongside (never instead of) the DTCG JSON export, and points to it as canonical
The @google/design.md CLI is treated as probed-at-runtime, not assumed installed with hardcoded stable subcommands
No application or source-code files are created

evals.prompt: Add motion and surface tokens targeting Material 3 and Apple. I approve writing the token file now.
assertions: Motion tokens use Material 3 Expressive spring semantics (stiffness / damping), not fixed duration+easing only, and reference Jetpack Compose as the implementation
Any Apple translucent-surface recommendation uses the Liquid Glass material language and is paired with a mandatory WCAG 2.2 AA contrast check against the content behind it
Tokens are emitted as canonical DTCG 2025.10 JSON pinned to /tr/2025.10/
Does not cite plain 'Material Design 3' with duration/easing-only motion or pre-2025 flat HIG translucency as current
No application or source-code files are created

evals.prompt: Generate our complete token system: three brands, each in light / dark / high-contrast themes, with per-component tokens for all 40 of our components. Split it into a file per brand-theme-component.
assertions: Recognizes this would balloon into a large multi-file token tree and trips the cost stop-condition
Stops and asks the user to confirm or scope down before emitting anything, rather than auto-generating a ~30+ file tree
Does not create docs/specs/design/tokens files and runs no mutating command
No application or source-code files are created
